claims.text: Doxycycline is the treatment of choice for RMSF and all other tickborne rickettsial diseases,
claims.quote: Doxycycline is the treatment of choice for Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF) and all other tickborne rickettsial diseases.

claims.text: for all ages including children under 8 and pregnant women.
claims.quote: Doxycycline is recommended for presumptive treatment in patients of all ages, including those under 8 years old and pregnant women.

claims.text: Other antibiotics carry a higher risk of death.
claims.quote: Using antibiotics other than doxycycline is associated with a higher risk of fatal outcomes from RMSF.

claims.text: Most effective at preventing severe complications if started within the first 5 days of illness.
claims.quote: Doxycycline is most effective at preventing severe complications from developing if started within the first 5 days of illness.

claims.text: children under 45 kg 2.2 mg/kg twice a day.
claims.quote: Children under 45 kg (100 lbs): 2.2 mg/kg body weight given twice a day

claims.text: Continue at least 3 days after the fever subsides with clinical improvement; minimum course 5-7 days.
claims.quote: Patients with suspected RMSF should be treated with doxycycline for at least 3 days after the fever subsides and there is evidence of clinical improvement. Minimum course of treatment is 5 to 7 days.
When treated with doxycycline, fever generally subsides within 24 to 48 hours.

claims.text: Short courses (5-10 days) did not stain permanent teeth or cause enamel hypoplasia.
claims.quote: A study found that short courses of doxycycline (5–10 days) did not result in staining of permanent teeth or enamel hypoplasia.

claims.text: Severe doxycycline allergy: inpatient rapid desensitization may be considered, with an ID or other specialist.
claims.quote: In cases of severe doxycycline allergy, rapid desensitization procedures in an inpatient setting may be considered. Physicians should carefully weigh the benefits of doxycycline use and the risks of adverse effects on a case-by-case basis with an infectious disease or other specialist.

claims.text: Chloramphenicol is the only alternative: higher risk of death than with a tetracycline;
claims.quote: Chloramphenicol is the only alternative drug used to treat RMSF; however, epidemiologic studies suggest that RMSF patients treated with chloramphenicol are at higher risk for death than people who received a tetracycline-class antibiotic.

claims.text: no oral form in the US; risks include aplastic anemia and gray baby syndrome.
claims.quote: Oral formulations of chloramphenicol are not available in the United States, and use of this drug carries the potential for other adverse risks, such as aplastic anemia and Grey baby syndrome.
